# Lean formalisation and paper: translation table

<!-- generated by scripts/assumption_table.py; do not edit by hand -->

Numbers refer to the paper as compiled from `st_article.tex`, commit `bcd5e5f`.
Lean toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.37.0-rc1`.

## What is formalised

The analysis of the paper is derived in Lean from an explicit list of assumptions, all of
which are fields of four structures in `StDgdg/Setting.lean`:

* `Setting`: the spaces, operators and forms of the method and the discrete inequalities,
* `Weight`: a temporal weight `φ(t)` (instances: `φ ≡ 1` and `φ = e^{-σt}`),
* `ExpWeight`: the exponential weight with the temporal projection `Π_t`,
* `ErrorData`: exact solution, interpolant and discrete solution.

The derivations are checked by the Lean kernel. The assumptions themselves are not proven in
general; they are proven for three model problems (see below).

## Reading the Lean statements

* Spaces are abstract real vector spaces, operators are linear maps, and every `L²`-type
  inner product (and the Ghost penalty form) is a symmetric positive semidefinite bilinear
  form. Norms appear squared, as `b u u`.
* The paper states the discrete inequalities for one element or facet; in Lean they are
  summed over the active elements or facets of one time slab.
* Every hidden constant of `≲` is an explicit function of `C`, `γ_J`, `λ` (`Consts`) and
  `σ`, `c0`, `C_φ`, `C_s` (`WConsts`) only.
* Time slabs are numbered `0, …, N−1` (paper: `1, …, N`).
* An assumption without a membership condition (for all `v : X`) is a requirement on the
  choice of the space `X`, see the header of `Setting.lean`.

## The assumptions

### `Setting`

**Parameters and regimes**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `h_pos`, `τ_pos`, `α_nonneg`, `wInf_nonneg` | – | signs of `h`, `Δt`, `α`, `‖w‖_∞` |
| `τ_le_one`, `h_le` | Section 4.1 | the standing assumptions `Δt ≤ 1` and `h ≲ 1` |
| `caseD` | (4.2) | Case D |
| `caseC` | (4.3) | Case C |

**Spaces and operators**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `Wh_le_Ws` | – | `W_h` consists of functions which are piecewise polynomial in space |
| `dx_mem` | – | `∇u ∈ [W_h]^d` for `u ∈ W_h` (used where Lemma 4.3 and superapproximation are applied to `∇u`) |
| `Lh_mem` | (4.6) | `𝓛_h u ∈ W_h` for `u ∈ W_h` |
| `mat_Lc` | (4.6) | `𝓛 = ∂_t + w·∇` in Case C |
| `mat_dt`, `Lc_dt` | – | `‖w·∇v‖ ≤ ‖w‖_∞ ‖∇v‖` on `Q^n`, for the material derivative and for `𝓛` (`𝓛 = ∂_t` in Case D) |

**Monotonicity of the forms**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `Q_le_QT` | – | follows from `Q^n ⊆ 𝒬_T^n` |
| `FQ_le` | (3.7) | follows from the splitting of the active facets into stabilised and interior ones |
| `Fint_le_FQ` | (3.7) | follows from `F × I_n ⊆ closure Q^n` for interior facets |
| `FQw_le` | – | `\|w·n\| ≤ ‖w‖_∞` (a bound of the weight, not an inclusion) |

**Standard discrete inequalities**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `trace_up`, `trace_dn` | (4.1a) | first inequality, for both one-sided traces: pointwise `\|u_∓\|² ≤ \|u\|_{T₁}\|² + \|u\|_{T₂}\|²` on a facet (the upwind side may change within a facet), then the inequality on both neighbours and summation over the active facets. Stated for functions which are only piecewise polynomial in space (`Ws`), as it is applied to the remainder `Π_t(φu) − φu` |
| `trace_nfl` | (4.1a), Lemma 4.13 | the same applied to `∇v` and averaged over the two sides; no displayed counterpart, used in the proof of the lemma |
| `trace_time` | (4.1a), Lemma 4.4 | second inequality, summed: `Ω(t_n)` and `Ω(t_{n+1})` are covered by the active elements of slab `n`. For `W_h` only (polynomial in time) |
| `trace_time_cont` | (4.1c) | second inequality, summed in the same way; applied to the remainder and to the interpolation error |
| `trace_up_cont` | (4.1c) | first inequality, multiplied by `h`, upwind trace, summed over the active facets; applied to the interpolation error only |
| `inv_dx` | (4.1b) | first inequality, summed; for `Ws` |
| `Lc_inv` | (4.1b), Lemma 4.17 | inverse inequality for `𝓛` (in Case C with `‖w‖_∞ Δt ≲ h`), as used in the proof of the lemma |

**Ghost penalty**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `gp` | Lemma 4.3, Assumption 4.1 | the lemma, slab-wise; it rests on the assumption |
| `gp_inv_dx` | Lemma 4.6 | spatial part. An inverse inequality within the Ghost penalty form; it does not follow from `gp` and `inv_dx` (the polynomial extension commutes with `∇`) |
| `gp_facet` | Lemma 4.7 | the core step of the proof, slab-wise and unscaled: `‖[v]‖²` on the stabilised facets `≤ C h⁻¹ j_h^n(v,v)`. The lemma follows by multiplying with `α h⁻¹ + ‖w‖_∞` and summing |

**The discrete derivative `𝓛_h`**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `Lc_Lh` | (4.18a) | as stated (trivial in Case D) |
| `Lh_inv_grad` | (4.18b) | second inequality |
| `Lh_gp` | (4.18c) | as stated; contains the temporal part of Lemma 4.6. The volume term stems from the jump of `w_h` across a facet patch and is absent in Case D |
| `Lh_int_jump` | Lemma 4.11 | interior facet step of the proof, no displayed counterpart: `[𝓛_h u] = ∂_t[u] + w_h·[∇u]`; temporal inverse inequality on `F × I_n`, trace inequality for `∇u` and `‖w‖_∞ Δt ≲ h` |

**Integration by parts**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `ibp` | Lemma 4.12 | first display of the proof: space-time integration by parts on the cut prisms of one slab, summed over the elements (uses `div w = 0` and `w^*·n^* = 0` on the lateral boundary) |

### `Weight`

**The weight `φ = φ(t)`**

| Lean field | Paper | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| `σ_nonneg`, `c0_pos`, `Cφ_nonneg`, `c0_le_lo`, `c0_le_phi`, `phi_le_one`, `hi_le` | Lemma 4.15 | `c0 ≤ φ ≤ 1` and `M_n ≤ C_φ m_n` (proof of the lemma). For `e^{-σt}`: `c0 = e^{-σT}`, `C_φ = e` if `σ Δt ≤ 1` |
| `dx_M`, `up_M`, `dn_M`, `nfl_M`, `bot_M`, `top_M` | – | `φ` depends on `t` only: it commutes with spatial derivatives and traces and is a number on each time level |
| `mat_M`, `Lc_M` | – | product rule with `φ' = −σφ` |
| `Q_symm`, `j_symm`, `FQ_symm`, `FQw_symm` | – | multiplication by `φ` is symmetric |
| `Q_lo`, `j_lo`, `FQ_lo`, `FQw_lo`, `FQ_hi` | – | `m_n ≤ φ ≤ M_n` on slab `n` |
| `Q_contr`, `j_contr`, `FQ_contr`, `FQw_contr` | – | `φ² ≤ 1` |

## The results

| Paper | Lean | Form of the statement |
|---|---|---|
| Theorem 4.18 | `ExpWeight.inf_sup` (Stability.lean), `ExpWeight.inf_sup_product` (Solvability.lean), `ExpWeight.unique_solvability` (Solvability.lean) | `inf_sup` is (4.32) with squared norms: `‖ṽ‖²_j ≤ M² ‖u‖²_j` and `(B_h+J)(u,ṽ) ≥ ⅛ ‖u‖²_j`. `inf_sup_product` is the product form with `C_stab = 1/(8M)` and `ṽ ≠ 0` for `‖u‖_j ≠ 0`. Unique solvability needs `W_h` finite dimensional and `‖·‖_{𝒬_T}` definite on `W_h` |
| Lemma 4.12 | `Setting.CU_mc` (Continuity.lean) | an identity |
| Lemma 4.20 | `Setting.continuity` (Continuity.lean) | Young form `2 B_h(x,v) ≤ s K₁ ‖x‖²_* + s⁻¹ K₂ ‖v‖²_j` for all `s > 0` |
| Proposition 5.2 | `ExpWeight.strang` (Continuity.lean) | squared |
| Lemma 5.4 | `ErrorData.approx_D` (Apriori.lean), `ErrorData.approx_C` (Apriori.lean) | squared; Case C without using `‖w‖_∞ ≃ 1` and `h ≲ 1` |
| Theorem 5.5 | `ErrorData.apriori_D` (Apriori.lean), `ErrorData.apriori_C` (Apriori.lean), `ErrorData.apriori_C_paper` (Apriori.lean) | squared; `apriori_C_paper` is the form of the paper and has `‖w‖_∞ ≃ 1` as hypotheses |

## Validation examples

In each of the following models every assumption of `Setting`, `Weight` and `ExpWeight` is
proven in Lean (from Mathlib, without further assumptions):

| Folder | Model problem | Exercises in particular |
|---|---|---|
| `Ode/` | DG(1) in time for an ODE (no space) | integration by parts, trace and inverse inequalities in time, the weight `e^{-σt}`, superapproximation; also `ErrorData`, so that the a priori estimate holds without assumptions |
| `Cut1d/` | heat equation on a fixed interval, cut at arbitrary positions (Case D, `w = 0`) | Ghost penalty estimates uniformly in the cut position, spatial trace and inverse inequalities, facet splitting, Nitsche terms |
| `Move1d/` | convection-diffusion on a moving interval, constant `w > 0`, both regimes | integration by parts on moving cut elements, upwind facet terms, Ghost penalty with swept elements, `𝓛 = ∂_t + w ∂_x` |

Not covered by the examples: more than one space dimension, polynomial degrees above one,
a variable velocity (`w_h ≠ w`, a changing upwind side), and `ErrorData` in one space dimension.
